Evidence:
[1] According to the 2010 census, the city had a population of 99,685 (making it Iowa's third-largest city).
[2] It is on and named after the Des Moines River, which likely was adapted from the French colonial name, "Rivière des Moines," meaning "River of the Monks." The city's population was 203,433 as of the 2010 census.
[3] It is the principal city of the Union Micropolitan Statistical Area (population 28,961 according to 2010 Census), an (MSA) which includes all of Union County and which is further included in the greater Greenville-Spartanburg-Anderson, South Carolina Combined Statistical Area (population 1,266,995 according to the 2010 Census).
[4] The present marquee was erected by the Iowa Neon Sign Company of Des Moines in 1948.
